rules.statement: When decrypting a JWE, report every failure that depends on the encrypted key, the ciphertext or the authentication tag as one exception type with one uniform message and no inner exception.
rules.why: RFC 7516 §11.5 forbids distinguishing these causes. Distinct messages, exception types or inner exceptions become an oracle on the key encryption (Bleichenbacher, RFC 3218).
rules.check: Look for distinct error messages for CEK unwrap and ciphertext/tag failures, inner exceptions attached to the decryption failure, or CryptographicException/ArgumentException from key management escaping the decode call.

rules.statement: When a JWE encrypted key fails to unwrap (the call returns false, produces a CEK of the wrong length, or throws), fill the CEK buffer from RandomNumberGenerator and go on with content decryption so that the failure happens at tag verification.
rules.why: Throwing at the unwrap step returns earlier than a tag failure, and that timing difference reveals which step failed, as RFC 7516 §11.5 warns.
rules.check: Look for early returns or throws right after a failed key unwrap or a CEK length mismatch, where the code should substitute a random CEK and let the tag check fail.

rules.statement: Before unwrapping a JWE key, check that the recipient's key has the algorithm's key type and a legal key size, and report a mismatch as a caller configuration error (ArgumentException) apart from the uniform decryption failure.
rules.why: These checks depend only on the caller's key and never on the token, so precise errors here leak nothing and still let a misconfigured recipient be diagnosed.
rules.check: Check that key-type and key-size validation runs before the unwrap and does not depend on token contents. Also check that token-dependent failures are not reported as configuration errors.

rules.statement: Apply the uniform JWE decryption-failure handling to the compact serialization and to every recipient of the JSON serialization.
rules.why: An oracle on any one recipient path reopens the attack that RFC 7516 §11.5 guards against.
rules.check: Look for JSON-serialization recipient loops or alternate decode paths that surface unwrap errors differently from the compact path.
